description: Git token and deploy key never reach git. Root cause (from Ervisio docs/api/plugins.md, not reproducible here): the git-* commands are admin/adminUnlessGroup docker, so for a user who is not in the docker group (an administrator) they run on the ROOT bridge as root, while storeCredentials writes the .cred/.key files with sdk.files into '~/.config/ervisio/plugins/docker/git', a '~' folder that is always used with the user's own rights in the user's home. git (as root, HOME=/root or a sanitised environment) then looks for /root/.config/.../<name>.cred, the store helper finds nothing, askPass is disabled -> 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com'. The same path mismatch breaks the deploy key (ssh -i points at a missing file). Second deploy-key bug: plugins.writeFile creates files 0644, and OpenSSH ignores a private key it owns whose mode has group/other bits ('UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE'), so even when HOME matches the key is refused. Third latent issue: fsx adds {env} for a paired Ervisio server, while the git commands always run on this machine. Fix: store the credentials in an absolute folder inside the admin folder /opt/stacks (same identity rule as the admin git commands, so writer and reader are always the same account), lock their mode to 600 with a declared command, keep the old ~ location as a read-only fallback so existing stacks keep working, and tell 'no login was sent' apart from 'login refused'.
steps: scripts/gen-manifest.mjs: add `export const GIT_AUTH_DIR = '/opt/stacks/.ervisio-git'` (STACKS + '/.ervisio-git'). Change GIT so the credential options become, in this order: '-c','credential.helper=' ; '-c',`credential.helper=store --file ${GIT_AUTH_DIR}/{0}.cred` ; '-c',`credential.helper=store --file ${CRED}.cred` (legacy ~ location kept as fallback; git asks helpers in order) ; '-c',`core.sshCommand=ssh -i ${GIT_AUTH_DIR}/{0}.key -i ${CRED}.key -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` (ssh only warns about a missing -i file and tries the next) ; '-c','core.askPass='. Update the comment above GIT to explain why the absolute admin folder is used (admin commands may run as root on the root bridge, where ~ is root's home, while ~ file writes always use the user's home) and that the ~ entries are a fallback for stacks added before this fix.

scripts/gen-manifest.mjs: add two commands next to the git ones, both with `...priv` (admin, adminUnlessGroup docker) and short timeouts: (a) 'git-auth-init': argv ['install','-d','-m','2770','-g','docker', GIT_AUTH_DIR], no args, description 'Create the private folder of Git logins in /opt/stacks (root and the docker group only)'; (b) 'git-auth-lock': argv ['chmod','600','--',`${GIT_AUTH_DIR}/{0}`], args [{ pattern: '[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}\\.(cred|key)', maxLen: 67 }] (whole-match pattern, so no '/' or '..'), description 'Make a Git login file readable only by its owner (ssh refuses a key others can read)'. Make sure these new names are in the set the generator owns (they are, since ownCmds is built from `commands`).

Run `node scripts/gen-manifest.mjs` to regenerate plugin/manifest.json, then `node scripts/gen-manifest.mjs --check`. Do not hand-edit generated entries. No change is needed in capabilities.files: /opt/stacks is already an admin read/write folder; keep the '~/.config/ervisio/plugins/docker' write folder (settings and legacy cleanup use it).

src/api/git.ts: add `export const GIT_AUTH_DIR = `${STACKS_DIR}/.ervisio-git`` (import STACKS_DIR from ./compose) and keep the old folder as LEGACY_CRED_DIR = `${CONFIG_DIR}/git`. credPath/keyPath now return paths in GIT_AUTH_DIR; add legacy path helpers. Credential files must be read/written/removed with getSdk().files WITHOUT the paired-server env (git commands always run on this machine): add a small local helper (e.g. `const localFs = { write: (p,d) => getSdk().files.write(p,d), ... }` with the same retry behaviour as fsx if easy, else plain calls) instead of fsx for these paths.

src/api/git.ts storeCredentials(name, url, auth): removeCredentials(name) first (now removes new AND legacy files, ignoring errors); return for 'none'; call ensureStacksFolder(); ensure GIT_AUTH_DIR exists: try files.list(GIT_AUTH_DIR); when not found run exec('git-auth-init', []) and throw an Error with stderr when it exits non-zero; write the .cred (credentialLine) or .key (normalised as today) file; then exec('git-auth-lock', [`${name}.cred` or `${name}.key`]) and throw a clear Error (include stderr) if it fails, removing the written file first so a world-readable secret is not left behind. Order matters: write, then chmod.
src/api/git.ts removeCredentials(name): remove new and legacy .cred/.key, each with .catch(() => undefined).

src/api/gitMeta.ts explainGitError: split the auth case. 'could not read (Username|Password)' or 'terminal prompts disabled' -> new key 'git.err.noLogin' (git got no login at all: no Token chosen, or the saved login could not be read). 'Authentication failed|Invalid username or (password|token)|HTTP 40[13]|returned error: 40[13]' -> keep 'git.err.auth' (login sent and refused). Add 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE|bad permissions' -> new key 'git.err.keyPerm' before the ssh case. Keep the ssh/notFound/network/... order otherwise; make sure the 'Warning: Identity file ... not accessible' line from the legacy -i fallback on its own does not change the classification of an otherwise successful or differently failing call (it does not match any pattern today; keep it that way, and keep 'no such identity' mapping only if it does not catch that warning).

src/api/git.ts: when a git call fails with key 'git.err.noLogin' or 'git.err.ssh' and the caller knows the stack uses a token/deploy key, check whether the expected file exists in GIT_AUTH_DIR (files.list of GIT_AUTH_DIR, local, no env) and, if it is missing, throw GitError with key 'git.err.credMissing' instead. Implement minimally: give lsRemote/cloneStack/checkForUpdate an optional `auth?: 'none'|'token'|'ssh'` (cloneStack already has meta.auth; checkForUpdate has meta.auth; GitStackPage check() knows `auth`) and do the check in one helper. GitError may need a constructor overload or a static factory to set key/detail directly.

src/i18n/areas/automation.ts: add English and Italian strings for 'git.err.noLogin' (e.g. EN: 'No login reached the repository: git was asked for a username and had none. Choose Token or Deploy key; for an existing stack enter the login again.'), 'git.err.credMissing' (EN: 'The saved login of this stack could not be found on this server. Enter the token or deploy key again.'), 'git.err.keyPerm' (EN: 'ssh refused the deploy key file because other users could read it. Save the key again.'). Reword 'git.err.auth' to say the repository refused the login (EN: 'The repository refused the login. Check the username and that the token can read this repository.'). Update 'gitnew.secret.where' (EN and IT) so it no longer claims the private home folder: it is now saved on this server in /opt/stacks/.ervisio-git, readable only by the account that runs the Git commands (you, or root after the administrator unlock), never shown again. Follow the existing tone; no em dashes.

Update the header comments of src/api/git.ts (Secrets paragraph) to the new location and the reason. Check every other place that mentions the old folder (grep 'plugins/docker/git', 'private plugin folder', 'mode 600') including README.md, and update it. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry in the existing style under the newest/unreleased section: Git logins (token and deploy key) now reach git also when the commands run with administrator rights; files moved to /opt/stacks/.ervisio-git with mode 600; older stacks keep working; clearer messages for a missing login vs a refused one.

Check the other callers still compile and behave: src/views/GitStackPage.tsx (check(): pass auth to lsRemote), src/views/StackPage.tsx (removeCredentials), src/api/portainer.ts (cloneStack, and its `e.key === 'git.err.auth'` test for pt.git.needsLogin: also accept 'git.err.noLogin', which is what a skipped login now produces).

Tests in test/automation.test.ts: update the 'git commands carry the safety options' test so every git-* command (except git-version and the new git-auth-* ones, which are not git invocations) has, in order, 'credential.helper=', then 'credential.helper=store --file /opt/stacks/.ervisio-git/{0}.cred', then the legacy '~/.config/ervisio/plugins/docker/git/{0}.cred' helper, and a core.sshCommand containing '-i /opt/stacks/.ervisio-git/{0}.key' before the legacy -i. Add a test that git-auth-init and git-auth-lock exist, are admin with adminUnlessGroup 'docker', git-auth-lock's pattern accepts 'web.cred' and 'my-app.key' and rejects '../x.cred', 'a/b.key', 'x.txt', '.cred', '-x.key' (compile as ^(?:pattern)$). Add a test that GIT_AUTH_DIR exported by src/api/git.ts equals the folder used in the manifest argv (import from git.ts only if that module loads under test/register.mjs; otherwise export the constant from gitMeta.ts or compose-free module and import it there). Add explainGitError cases: 'fatal: could not read Username for \'https://github.com\': No such device or address' -> git.err.noLogin; 'remote: Invalid username or token.\nfatal: Authentication failed for ...' -> git.err.auth; 'Permissions 0644 for ... are too open.\n...UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!' -> git.err.keyPerm; a stderr with 'Warning: Identity file /home/u/.config/ervisio/plugins/docker/git/x.key not accessible: No such file or directory.' followed by 'Permission denied (publickey)' -> git.err.ssh. Update any existing assertion that expected 'git.err.auth' for 'could not read Username'.

Add a test (new file test/gitcreds.test.ts or inside automation.test.ts) that mocks the SDK with setSdk (pattern in test/followups.test.ts: an in-memory files map plus api.exec recording calls) and exercises storeCredentials: token case writes '/opt/stacks/.ervisio-git/<name>.cred' with the credentialLine content, runs 'git-auth-init' when the folder is missing and not when it exists, then runs 'git-auth-lock' with ['<name>.cred'] after the write; ssh case writes '<name>.key' and locks it; a failing git-auth-lock removes the written file and rejects; files calls carry no env option; removeCredentials removes both new and legacy paths. Also test the credMissing mapping: lsRemote with auth 'token' when exec returns exitCode 128 and the 'could not read Username' stderr and no .cred in the folder -> GitError key 'git.err.credMissing'. If stacksFolderExists/ensureStacksFolder need files.list('/opt/stacks') to succeed, have the mock return [] for it.
Run node scripts/gen-manifest.mjs --check, npm run typecheck, npm test; fix failures. Try npm run build and report the result.

Follow-up (review): the legacy ~ helper was `store --file ~/...{0}.cred`, which git also calls with store/erase, so a successful token login copied the token into the ~ folder of the account running git (root for an admin), never cleaned up by removeCredentials. Replaced in scripts/gen-manifest.mjs by LEGACY_HELPER = `!f() { [ "$1" != get ] || git credential-store --file ${CRED}.cred get; }; f` (read-only, store/erase exit 0), comment above GIT explains why; hand-mirrored into all 8 git-* argv in plugin/manifest.json as "credential.helper=!f() { [ \"$1\" != get ] || git credential-store --file ~/.config/ervisio/plugins/docker/git/{0}.cred get; }; f"; test/automation.test.ts now looks up that exact item, asserts it starts with 'credential.helper=!' and contains '[ "$1" != get ] ||', and that the old store ~ helper is absent (the 'ext' / protocol.file check still holds). CHANGELOG and the src/api/git.ts header comment mention the read-only fallback. Still unverified (shell DriveNotFoundException): gen-manifest --check, typecheck, tests. No commit. Follow-up 2 (review 2026-10-03-120000): issue 1, the EN+IT git.err.noLogin/credMissing/keyPerm messages and the CHANGELOG no longer say 'enter the login again' (no screen for it); they say a login is entered only in New stack from Git, so delete the stack and add it again there, or detach it from Git and add it under another name (detachStack keeps the folder, so the same name would hit git.err.exists). No 'change login' screen was built. Issue 2, src/api/git.ts loginFileMissing now lists GIT_AUTH_DIR and then LEGACY_CRED_DIR with localFs: a matching file in either -> false; a list error other than isNotFound (e.g. needs_admin) -> false (original git error kept); only both folders known to lack the file -> true (credMissing). test/gitcreds.test.ts: mock got state.lsStderr and state.listFail (throws code needs_admin), keyOf moved to module level, new tests 'deploy key kept in the old folder and refused stays git.err.ssh' (then credMissing once the legacy key is removed) and 'login folder that cannot be listed' (needs_admin on GIT_AUTH_DIR or on LEGACY_CRED_DIR -> git.err.noLogin). Issue 3, documented only: modes stay 600 for .cred and .key; CHANGELOG now says each login file belongs to the account that saved it and Check/Update work for that account and for scheduled jobs (which run as the stack's owner). Rationale for keeping .cred at 600: a token is a secret like the key, and widening it would need a group-chmod command plus a second pattern; the not-a-regression case (a second docker-group user) is rare.
